item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
I'm no lawyer, but even I know that's not how "fair use" works.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_use#1._Purpose_and_character_of_the_use

Even a summary on wikipedia states that being transformative is one of the most important considerations in whether something qualifies as fair use although it isn't the be-all end-all. The additional considerations listed there also make it sound pretty solid, considering, for instance that one can hardly talk about the detriment to the original holder's ability to exploit their… illustrative image of a bowel section.

Also, while I thank your efforts (and some of the images you've found are indeed amazing) it misses the point slightly since the article was written by someone else- my contribution was the image edit.

item.title: Operational Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
If an author owned an image, they are free to PM staff about it and we will be more than happy to restore the image. Currently, only the image coding is removed; the image files still remain.

CSS is not subject to copyright.

Please direct any other questions, comments, or concerns to the Licensing Team Captain ProcyonLotor.

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Nope. The image to SCP-173 was and could be clearly sourced (and with a license that was an actual issue) and any concerns the wiki needs to have begin at that point.

Considering that a thing that is, in fact created and appears somewhere for the first time can't indeed be sourced via lookup makes the assumption that anything that can't be sourced is stolen seem absurd - furthermore it's inconsistent with the wiki policies elsewhere. After all, we have had a case of text plagiarism with the Meeps, too - what you're doing with images is akin to deleting every SCP whose text's provenience can't be determined because it wasn't proven that it's its author's original creation.

This gets even sillier with the actual case of plagiarism of CSS sheets that's happened before where the staff stance which I still can probably document was along the lines of "the fact this appears to be the same in two places isn't proof that it was plagiarized because the OP might not have created the code either" which was not only absurd in its own way, but, completely at odds with the stance taken with images.

So yeah, this isn't erring on the side of caution as much as pouring the baby out with the bathwater.

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
one would think staff would err on the side of caution

We are. We’ve already had cases where images used on the site were not released under CC 3.0 or otherwise stolen wholesale from their original copyright — most notably SCP-173. Making sure that every image is explicitly compliant with our site license is being cautious.

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Reverted this absurd change since I'm the author of the second picture, assembled from a bunch of stock pictures and about an hour of GIMP.

Needless to say, this fact shows exactly the problem with a policy of offhand, quiet removal of pictures that "can't be sourced", especially since a lot of the people who occassionally made images are not around anymore.

One would think staff would err on the side of caution.

Title: Amazon rainforest near Puerto Maldonado

The second image that was used in this article could not be found under any source as cc-compliant. Thus, it is assumed that the image is non-compliant with the SCP wiki's license (CC BY-SA 3.0) and has been removed.
